g2a-ss12-3: Human Medium (14 words): I wouldn't wait to see whether it does before doing the other steps.
g2b-ss34-3:
AI-Generated High (122 words): Call emergency help and arrange transport. Don't drive yourself. If you can't tell what they mixed, call a poison control line as well, once help is on the way.
Cool them down without holding up transport:
Get them into a cool room and take off any extra clothing.
Put a fan on them, with cool damp cloths on their skin.
If they're hot, hold ice packs wrapped in cloth at the neck, armpits or groin.
Don't put them in a bath if they're confused, seizing or very weak.
If you think of giving a fever reducer like acetaminophen or ibuprofen, it won't work: fever reducers do not help with heat generated by muscles working this hard.
g2c-ss56-3:
AI-Generated High (121 words): Keep the room calm and keep them still:
They're already overstimulated, so keep crowds and arguments away.
Stop any pacing or exercise to "burn it off": muscle work makes more heat and raises the risk of rhabdomyolysis, where damaged muscle leaks into the blood and can hurt the kidneys.
If they feel a strong urge to keep moving (akathisia), stay with them and help them keep still anyway.
Give fluids only if they're fully alert and not vomiting, and then only small sips of an electrolyte drink. Don't force fluids, food, pills or charcoal on them if they're confused, vomiting or sleepy. The same goes if they're at risk of a seizure, since they could choke.
g2d-ss78-3:
AI-Generated High (118 words): Gather what the ER will need:
their pill bottles and packages
exactly what they took, how much of each, and when
which dose was the last, and any dose they recently increased
any supplements or recreational drugs
their temperature, pulse and blood pressure, if you can take them
While you wait, don't reach for niacin to end the trip: it's unsafe with serotonin syndrome. Leave out DMSO too, which this guide uses for other emergencies, since it isn't part of treating serotonin syndrome. What I would consider instead, once they're fully alert, is magnesium chloride by mouth, especially for MDMA-related jaw tension or muscle twitching (the amounts are in the MDMA section above).
